questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Fundamental Vector Product of a Parametric Surface
questions.problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z=u-{e}^{v}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-{e}^{v}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-{e}^{v})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-{e}^{v}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -{e}^{v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -{e}^{v}\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -{e}^{v}\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,{e}^{v},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,-v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v+uv\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u,\,y=v,\,z={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2u \\ 0 & 1 & -2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2u \\ 1 & -2v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2u \\ 0 & -2v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u,\,2v,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,{v}^{2},\,4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,0,\,-4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(\operatorname{sin}⁡u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(4v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡u & 0 & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & 2v & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 2v & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡u & -4v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & 4\operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨8{v}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,-4{cos}^{2}⁡u,\,2v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={u}^{2}+1,\,y={v}^{3}+1,\,z=2u+v.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}+1,\,{v}^{3}+1,\,2u+v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,3{v}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2}\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6{v}^{2},\,-2u,\,6u{v}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface
questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le \pi }
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u⟩$ for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le \pi .$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡v & 1 \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡v & 1 \\ -3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 1 \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-6u{sin}^{2}⁡v-6u{cos}^{2}⁡v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-6u⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-6u⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)^{2}+(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)^{2}+(-6u)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v)+4{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v)+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+40{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡v+8)} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡v+8} \\  & =\sqrt{5}u\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡v+8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{u}^{2}}=u$ since $u\ge 0$ on $D.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{5}u\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡v+8}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,3-v,\,1+4u+5v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 2.$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+4u+5v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,4⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+4u+5v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-1,\,-1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨4,\,-1,\,-1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(4)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{18} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,0\le v\le \pi }
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 4$ and $0\le v\le \pi .$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & {e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & {e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ 0 & {e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & {e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ {e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & {e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ 0 & -{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & {e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ 0 & {e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{2u}({sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v),\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{2u},\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-{e}^{2u},\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-{e}^{2u})^{2}+({e}^{u}\operatorname{sin}⁡v)^{2}+({e}^{u}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{4u}+{e}^{2u}{sin}^{2}⁡v+{e}^{2u}{cos}^{2}⁡v} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{4u}+{e}^{2u}({sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v)} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{4u}+{e}^{2u}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2u}({e}^{2u}+1)} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2u}}\sqrt{{e}^{2u}+1} \\  & ={e}^{u}\sqrt{{e}^{2u}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{e}^{u}\sqrt{{e}^{2u}+1}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & v \\ 0 & 2v & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & v \\ 2v & u\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & v \\ 0 & u\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-2{u}^{2},\,4uv⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-2{u}^{2},\,4uv⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-2{v}^{2})^{2}+(-2{u}^{2})^{2}+(4uv)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{4}+4{u}^{4}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({u}^{4}+{v}^{4}+4{u}^{2}{v}^{2})} \\  & =2\sqrt{{u}^{4}+{v}^{4}+4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\sqrt{{u}^{4}+{v}^{4}+4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2v,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2v & 2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2v & 2v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 1 \\ 0 & -2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,-4uv,\,-4uv⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2v,\,-4uv,\,-4uv⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2v)^{2}+(-4uv)^{2}+(-4uv)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+32{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}(1+8{u}^{2})} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}}\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}} \\  & =2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{v}^{2}}=v$ since $v\ge 0$ on $D.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}

$$
x=2u-v,\,y=3u+2,\,z=u+2v
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $-1\le v\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u-v,\,3u+2,\,u+2v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3u+2),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3u+2),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-5,\,3⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨6,\,-5,\,3⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+25+9} \\  & =\sqrt{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, let's denote

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,-1\le v\le 1}.
$$

Then, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{70}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}{∬}_{D}\text{ }\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\sqrt{70}\cdot 1\cdot 2 \\  & =2\sqrt{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1-2u+5v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1-2u+5v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-5,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2,\,-5,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(-5)}^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+25+1} \\  & =\sqrt{30}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that the region ${u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 2$ corresponds to the disk

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 2}
$$

of radius $\sqrt{2}.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{30}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{30}{∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{30}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\sqrt{30}\cdot (\pi \cdot (\sqrt{2})^{2}) \\  & =2\pi \sqrt{30}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y=uv,\,z=\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $1\le v\le 2.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,uv,\,\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,v,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u,\,v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & v & 0 \\ 0 & u & v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}v & 0 \\ u & v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & v \\ 0 & u\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨{v}^{2},\,-2uv,\,2{u}^{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨{v}^{2},\,-2uv,\,2{u}^{2}⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({v}^{2})^{2}+(-2uv)^{2}+(2{u}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{v}^{4}+4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+4{u}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{({v}^{2}+2{u}^{2})^{2}} \\  & ={v}^{2}+2{u}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, let's denote

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,1\le v\le 2}.
$$

Then, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}({v}^{2}+2{u}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}({v}^{2}+2{u}^{2})\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[u{v}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3}]}_{0}^{1}\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}({v}^{2}+\frac{2}{3})\text{d}v \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{v}^{3}+\frac{2}{3}v]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[{2}^{3}+2(2)-({1}^{3}+2(1))] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(9) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u^2, \: v^2, \: u+v \big\rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $\mathbf r (u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2v & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2v & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2v,\,-2u,\,4uv⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065243/assets/95e3f2da04e23c9b42ea04cba3ee1d7cc069fef992592f09a70cef367b670f0d.png)

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u, \: v, \: u^3-v \big\rangle$ for $0 \leq u \leq 3$ and $0 \leq v \leq 2.$ What is the missing expression?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf r (u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \,\textrm d S = \iint\limits_D  \left\|  \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \right\|  \text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3{u}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-3{u}^{2},\,1,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and its magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-3{u}^{2},\,1,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(3{u}^{2})^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{u}^{4}+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{9{u}^{4}+2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
